Curious how does someone survive without a Large Intestine? Seems like an extreme measure to take.

Your large intestine is essentially limited in function to re-absorption of water as well as uptake of things like potassium, but it's not the only part of the body that does either of those functions. Essentially, what happened for me was the my Ulcerative Colitis stopped responding to medication and would have likely led to colon cancer and a worse state than removal of the intestine. In my case they created a make-shift colon from the end of my small intestine to act as a pouch (it's called a J-Pouch) so that I could go to the bathroom normally. If that fails or if someone is not able to have that pouch made, they will instead have a permanent Ostomy bag. I had an ostomy for 3 months between surgeries. Life is pretty normal, there are some weird health things that continue to be a problem, but it's orders of magnitude better than it used to be.
